passages.title: How to stay safe in extreme cold
passages.text:
In winter, temperatures in many parts of Mongolia fall below minus 30 °C. In such conditions, the human body loses heat very quickly, and serious problems such as frostbite can develop in less than half an hour. Frostbite happens when skin and the tissue under it freeze. It usually affects the fingers, toes, nose and ears first.

Before you go out …
• Wear several thin layers of clothing rather than one thick layer. Air between the layers keeps you warm.
• Cover your head, hands and face. A lot of body heat is lost through the head.
• Eat a hot meal. Your body needs energy to produce heat.

When you are outside …
• Keep moving, but don't sweat too much. If your clothes get wet, **<u>they</u>** stop keeping you warm.
• Check your friends' faces. White or grey patches on the skin are an early sign of frostbite.

If someone has frostbite, take the person indoors and warm the area slowly with warm, not hot, water. Never rub frozen skin with snow; this old method can damage the skin even more.

sourceNote: 2022–2026 оны жишиг эх нь албан БҮТ-ийн эх биш, нийтэд нээлттэй хуулбар; 2018–2020 оны албан хувилбарын бүтцийг баримталсан.
